cards.text: Paul's letter to the believers in Rome is almost done (Romans 1:1, 7), and now he's saying goodbye. If you've ever tried to leave a family party, you know goodbyes take a WHILE. First up, he commends Phoebe, a sister in the faith and a servant of the church in Cenchrea.

cards.question: Phoebe is coming from the church in Cenchrea. What does Paul tell the believers in Rome to do for her?

answers.text: Welcome her and help with anything she needs
Send her straight on to Jerusalem
Find her a ship headed for Spain

cards.question: Paul says Phoebe has been a great ___ to many people, including him.

cards.text: Next, Paul says to greet Prisca and Aquila, his fellow workers in Christ Jesus, and these two went WAY past the job description. Back in the junk drawer, the most the rubber bands I bunked with ever did for me was not snap.

cards.question: Prisca and Aquila are Paul's fellow workers. What did they do for Paul?

answers.text: They risked their lives for him
They gave him all their savings
They nursed him through an illness

cards.question: Paul is the only one grateful to Prisca and Aquila.
Right after Prisca and Aquila, Paul greets a church. Where does that church meet?

cards.text: Then Paul greets his beloved Epenetus, from the province of Asia. Paul says "beloved" the way I say "friend," and friend, I say it a LOT.

cards.question: Epenetus was the ___ convert to Christ in the province of Asia.

cards.text: Then Paul greets Mary, who has worked very hard for them. Next come Andronicus and Junia, his fellow countrymen and fellow prisoners, and Paul says they are outstanding among the apostles.

cards.question: Paul says Andronicus and Junia came to Christ after he did.

cards.text: Then the names just KEEP COMING: beloved friends, fellow workers, whole households and women who have worked hard in the Lord. The standout is Rufus's mother, who has been a mother to Paul as well, and as a stamper who ended up Papa to six little cookie cutters, I RESPECT that.

cards.question: After all those names, Paul tells the believers in Rome to greet one another. How?

answers.text: With a bow of the head

cards.question: Paul tells the believers in Rome that all the churches of Christ send them greetings.

cards.text: Then Paul's tone shifts, and he urges them to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles contrary to the teaching they have learned. I gave every newcomer to the junk drawer the same kind of heads-up: "Glad you're here, friend, and stay AWAY from the twist tie, because that thing will tangle up the WHOLE drawer."

cards.question: Paul tells the believers in Rome what to do about people who create divisions. What is it?

cards.text: Paul says these people are not serving our Lord Christ. And he says they have a way of fooling the naive.

cards.question: The people who cause divisions aren't serving our Lord Christ. Who are they serving instead?
Paul warns that the people who cause divisions fool the naive with loud threats.

cards.text: Their trick is smooth talk and flattery. Friend, when somebody tells me my chef's hat looks EXTRA tall today, I already know they're after the last batch.
Then Paul turns to the believers in Rome themselves. Everyone has heard about their obedience, so he rejoices over them.

cards.question: Paul wants the believers in Rome to be wise about what is ___ and innocent about what is ___.
Paul says that the God of peace will soon crush Satan under the believers' feet.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you." And just when it sounds like goodbye, the people with him start sending greetings too, beginning with Timothy, his fellow worker.
Lucius, Jason and Sosipater, Paul's fellow countrymen, send greetings as well. Then a brand new voice speaks up in the letter to greet them in the Lord: Tertius.

cards.question: A new voice in Paul's letter greets the believers in Rome. Who is Tertius?

answers.text: The one who wrote down this letter
The one who will carry this letter
The leader of the church in Rome

cards.text: Tertius writes down this WHOLE letter and gets ONE line to say hi, like the coworker who types up the entire report and gets thanked at the very bottom. Then even more greetings roll in.

cards.question: Gaius sends the believers in Rome greetings. What is Gaius known for?
Erastus, the city ___, sends greetings, and so does our brother Quartus.

cards.text: And Paul goes out BIG, with praise to Him who is able to strengthen them by Paul's gospel and the proclamation of Jesus Christ. Then Paul brings up a mystery concealed for ages past.

cards.question: Paul says the mystery concealed for ages past stays hidden.
Paul says the mystery is made known through the writings of the prophets, to lead all ___ to the obedience that comes from faith.
Paul ends the whole letter with glory forever to the only wise God. Through whom?

findings.problem: Paul shows up for the first time in this lesson on the opening card, but nothing says who he is (for example, an apostle, per the cited Romans 1:1). The card only says "Paul's letter."

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke adds a new detail to the junk drawer backstory: the rubber bands he "bunked with," and that the most they ever did for him was not snap. The drawer is not his bakery, so this is new backstory. It also makes light of the drawer friends he says he was "all in it together" with.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The joke invents new junk drawer backstory: Papa Dorin warning newcomers to stay away from the twist tie because it tangles up the whole drawer. This adds to the drawer story, which is not his bakery. It also casts one of his drawer friends as a divider like the false teachers. That conflicts with "They were all in it together" and with his kindness toward them.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: This true or false card about the God of peace crushing Satan comes straight after the fill in the blank on verse 19. No earlier card gives any context for verse 20, so the baker has nothing to reason from and the pick comes down to luck.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Through the prophets" is not false in the passage. Verse 26 says the mystery is made known "through the writings of the prophets," and card 18 just told the baker that. A baker could argue for it.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: Verses 8 to 15 are treated as a name list and summed up in one card. Verses 3 to 7 are the same kind of greeting list, but they get choice cards on small details: card 9 (Epenetus was the first convert in Asia, 16:5) and card 11 (Andronicus and Junia were in Christ before Paul, 16:7). The docs list "genealogies and name lists" as long stretches that never get choice cards. They don't say whether a greeting list with a short description on each name counts, or where such a stretch begins.
findings.question: Does Paul's greeting list in Romans 16:3-16 count as a long stretch (a name list)? If it does, should only the standout moments, like Phoebe's commendation and Prisca and Aquila risking their lives, get choice cards, with detail cards like 9 and 11 folded into a summary?
